name: Raffles Makati
positioning: All-suite Raffles hotel in Makati's Central Business District, with an Authors-in-Residence programme and Raffles Residences for longer stays
best_for: Travelers who want an all-suite base in Makati's Central Business District
Readers drawn to the hotel's Authors-in-Residence programme
Longer stays in residential units with kitchens and laundry areas

facts.text: Raffles Makati is at 1 Raffles Drive, Makati Avenue, in Makati's Central Business District.
The hotel is within walking distance of the Zuellig Building and the Ayala Museum.
The 30-storey complex that houses Raffles Makati opened to guests on 3 December 2012.
Raffles Makati is an all-suite hotel.
Each suite has floor-to-ceiling windows framing views of the Makati cityscape.
Suites feature curated artwork from the Hotel Art collection.
Raffles Residences Makati has residential units with kitchens and laundry areas furnished for long stays.
Mirèio, on the 9th floor, serves French and Mediterranean cuisine.
Mistral Rooftop Bar serves artisanal cocktails with views of Makati's sunsets.
The Writers Bar and Long Bar are on the lobby level.
The spa's signature treatments highlight traditional Filipino techniques.
Authors the hotel has hosted include Mitch Albom and Amy Tan.

highlights.text: Mirèio is named after an 1859 poem by Nobel Laureate Frédéric Mistral, a tribute to his native Provence.
In 2013 the hotel started an Authors-in-Residence programme in partnership with the National Bookstore.
In 2014 the hotel hosted the first Philippine Readers and Writers Festival.
The Raffles Pool is on the 9th floor and is exclusively for Raffles guests.
All suites and residences include breakfast, served in Mirèio or Spectrum.

considerations.text: Arrival from Manila Ninoy Aquino International Airport is by taxi.
WhataHotel notes an urban business district setting.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the ultra-luxury positioning.
